title: Continuous Physical Substrate of Neural Information Processing. From Transduction to Effection
content: A theory of neural computation has to answer to the tissue that carries it. We ask what physical medium neural computation plausibly runs on. Sensory information enters as a continuous physical quantity and motor information leaves the same way, so whatever sits between the two must either preserve that continuity or restore it losslessly at every interface. The argument is presented as a reductio hypothesis: making the intermediate substrate binary would leave every interface demanding lossless reconstruction as a liability that, on this reading, no biological interface has been documented paying. The substrate is proposed as analog from end to end. This requirement is read here as two coupled tasks, transmission and reconstruction, that one physical medium can perform. Messages from many fibres converge onto a shared gel and interfere there. The oscillation and coherence documented in the textbook are read as this interference figure rather than as hidden clocks, and the same medium reads out as the discriminatory field at the sensory end. Deeper in the brain, what the substrate does precisely remains an open question; what is proposed is that it stays continuous and fluidic, so no encoding step is asked of it. The Ionic-Mechano-Hydraulic framework names the candidate medium: the periaxonal gel, graded synaptic transmission, and the matrix-borne neurotag, framed as one continuous network. It generates falsifiable predictions at every scale, from a small reversible heat signature to atomic force microscopy of the living gel.
